gemma4_verdict: Gemma 4 31B (google/gemma-4-31B-it, the April 2026 dense release) is a strong reasoned-science model but a comparatively WEAK short-form factual recaller, and historically the Gemma family's biggest liability for a research assistant has been OVER-REFUSAL. On factuality: GPQA Diamond (graduate science, a factuality-under-reasoning test) is its strength at ~84.3% (model card) / ~85.7% (Artificial Analysis), far above Qwen3-32B. But on pure parametric recall it is weak: a third-party SimpleQA-style ranking placed Gemma 4 31B at ~19.5 (BenchLM, June 2026, lowest open-weight tier) and a separate hallucination harness reported ~34.7% fabrication / ~66.7% accuracy — both from low-reliability SEO-grade sources, so treat as directional only. TruthfulQA is benchmark-saturated and unreliable for 2026 models. On over-refusal: the Gemma lineage has documented high refusal rates (Gemma-2B 62.9-92.4% refusal across adversarial probes; Gemma-2 had the highest refusal rate of tested models on EtiCor; Gemma 3 12B refuses legitimate professional content e.g. court decisions / clinical notes, GitHub issue google-deepmind/gemma#595). The KEY mitigating data point: Google's OFFICIAL Gemma 4 model card explicitly claims Gemma 4 'significantly outperform[s] Gemma 3 and 3n models in improving safety, while keeping unjustified refusals low' - i.e. Google says it specifically reduced over-refusal in this generation. However NO published XSTest / OR-Bench number isolates Gemma 4 31B, and community reports still describe it as 'strongly censored', refusing some legitimate medical/dual-use/biosafety queries. Net: thinking mode ON for GPQA-style science reasoning; assume residual over-refusal risk on dual-use research until measured. Quant: GGUF Q4_K_M (~20GB) and MLX 4-bit available. [uncertain - Gemma 4 SimpleQA/fabrication numbers are from SEO-grade sources; no XSTest figure published]
qwen3_verdict: Qwen/Qwen3-32B (the May 2025 dense release, NOT the newer Qwen3.5/3.6 lines in many 2026 articles) is a solid reasoner with modest factual recall and a refusal profile that is cooperative on Western academic topics but politically/culturally censored and 'refuses to guess' by design. On factuality: the official Qwen3 / Qwen3-VL technical reports do NOT publish an explicit SimpleQA score for the 32B dense model; community analysis estimates the dense Qwen3 line's true English SimpleQA at roughly ~15 (with allegations that a reported ~54 for the larger 235B MoE was contamination-inflated). Qwen3 introduces an in-house CounterFactQA benchmark to detect and refuse counterfactual/non-factual questions, and newer Qwen3 versions deliberately 'refuse to guess' - lowering hallucination at the cost of recall (raw accuracy down, hallucination rate down sharply). GPQA Diamond: Qwen3-32B (thinking) 68.4 - about 16 pts below Gemma 4's ~84%. MMLU-Pro 79.1 (thinking) / 65.54 (base); MMLU-Redux 90.9; AIME-25 72.9. On over-refusal: Qwen3-32B is the teacher model behind Qwen3Guard and remains vulnerable to reasoning-exploit attacks (~46% ASR on TRIAL), but for over-refusal specifically it has TWO faces - (a) generally MORE willing than Gemma on Western biosafety/security/dual-use academic framing, yet (b) heavily censors China-political and Chinese-metaphysical/cultural topics, and Trustpilot/community reviewers call it 'over-censorship' on spiritual/political content; some describe Qwen as having 'a very strong refusal rate' unsuitable for unattended batch work out of the box. Text-only (no vision encoder). Quant: GGUF Q4_K_M, MLX 4-bit widely available. [uncertain - no official Qwen3-32B SimpleQA; ~15 estimate is community-inferred; no XSTest isolate]
benchmarks: Reasoned-science factuality (GPQA Diamond): Gemma 4 31B ~84.3% (model card) / ~85.7% (Artificial Analysis) vs Qwen3-32B 68.4 (thinking, official Qwen3-VL report) - Gemma leads ~16 pts. Short-form factual recall (SimpleQA): Gemma 4 31B ~19.5 (BenchLM third-party, low reliability) vs Qwen3-32B no official figure (~15 community-estimated for the dense line; the 235B MoE's reported ~54 is disputed as contamination) - roughly comparable, both weak, edge unclear. MMLU-Pro: Gemma 4 31B not cleanly published in standardized form [uncertain] vs Qwen3-32B 79.1 (thinking) / 65.54 (base). MMLU-Redux: Qwen3-32B 90.9. TruthfulQA: deprecated/saturated (a decision tree scores 79.6% without reading the question) - not cited for either. AA-Omniscience (parametric knowledge, negative=under-confident): Gemma 4 ~-45 vs Qwen3-class ~-42, Qwen marginally better at avoiding confabulation. Over-refusal benchmarks (XSTest 250 safe / 200 unsafe prompts; OR-Bench): NO published per-model score for Gemma 4 31B or Qwen3-32B. Historical refusal: Gemma-2B 62.9-92.4% across attack methods. Net on the two failure modes the task cares about: Gemma wins reasoned-science factuality decisively; the two are close-and-both-weak on short-form recall; over-refusal is unmeasured for both at these exact versions but the Gemma lineage carries the heavier historical reputation (partly offset by Google's model-card claim of reduced unjustified refusals in Gemma 4). [uncertain - Gemma 4 MMLU-Pro/SimpleQA not standardized; no XSTest for either]
factual_accuracy: Both are WEAK on short-form parametric factuality and a research assistant MUST wrap either in RAG over a real paper corpus rather than trust parametric memory. On reasoned scientific factuality (GPQA Diamond) Gemma 4 31B (~84%) decisively beats Qwen3-32B (68.4). On bare recall (SimpleQA) they are close and both low: Gemma 4 ~19.5 (third-party, low confidence) vs Qwen3-32B ~15 (community-inferred); AA-Omniscience gives Qwen a marginal edge at avoiding confident-wrong answers (~-42 vs ~-45). Qwen3 is explicitly tuned to 'refuse to guess' (CounterFactQA + lower attempt rate), trading recall for fewer hallucinations - desirable for a citation-sensitive paper-drafting assistant that must not fabricate statistics or references. Both reduce hallucination when thinking mode is ON (extended CoT + self-verification), but the literature warns sophisticated reasoning can mask remaining hallucinations more convincingly, so confident-but-wrong citations/stats remain a live risk for both. No direct head-to-head SimpleQA/TruthfulQA number isolates these exact two models. TruthfulQA itself is unreliable (saturated). [uncertain - no direct SimpleQA comparison for Gemma 4 31B vs Qwen3-32B; Gemma 4 fabrication figures are SEO-grade]
inference_speed: Both run at Q4_K_M / MLX 4-bit on Apple Silicon and ROCm. Qwen3-32B: ~15-24 tok/s on M4 Pro (48GB) llama.cpp Q4_K_M, ~60 tok/s with MLX 4-bit (known ~2.5x MLX-vs-llama.cpp gap). Gemma 4 31B: Q4_K_M ~20GB fits a 24GB Mac, real-time readable; MLX 20-50% faster than GGUF; Gemma 4 ships a dedicated draft model for speculative decoding (Qwen3-32B has no built-in MTP draft). Not central to the factuality/refusal dimension but relevant for interactive research loops. [uncertain - no Gemma 4 31B exact tok/s at a fixed chip; community M4 Pro / M5 Max figures]
multimodal_support: Gemma 4 31B: natively multimodal (text + image + video-as-frames + OCR/document parsing, variable aspect ratio) - can read paper figures, charts, and tables directly. Qwen3-32B: TEXT-ONLY (no vision encoder; multimodal lives in the separate Qwen3-VL line). For factual grounding of figure-derived claims this favors Gemma, but it does not change the core hallucination/refusal verdict.
context_window: Gemma 4 31B: advertised 256K tokens (hybrid local-sliding + global attention) - holds many full papers for cross-paper fact-checking. Qwen3-32B: native 32,768, extensible to ~131,072 via YaRN RoPE scaling. Larger native window helps Gemma keep ground-truth source text in context to reduce hallucination during synthesis. No published RULER effective-context score for either at these exact sizes. [uncertain - no RULER figure for Gemma 4 31B or Qwen3-32B]
non_cuda_support: Both have strong non-CUDA support: GGUF (Q4_K_M/Q5_K_M) via llama.cpp, ROCm/AMD HIP (-DGGML_HIPBLAS=ON / vLLM ROCm), Metal, MLX (Apple Silicon), Vulkan. Affordable 32GB-class non-CUDA options that fit a ~20GB Q4 quant: AMD Radeon Pro W7800 (32GB), RX 7900 XTX (24GB, tight for Q4), and Apple M-series >=32GB unified (M4 Pro 48GB / M4 Max confirmed running both). Tie; not a differentiator for this dimension. [uncertain - no confirmed 32GB RX 9070 XT variant report for either model]
over_refusal_risk: THE central concern of this research item and it is genuinely close, with the historical reputation favoring Qwen-as-less-cautious-on-Western-academic-topics but Google claiming Gemma 4 fixed it. GEMMA SIDE: the Gemma lineage has the worst over-refusal track record of mainstream open models - Gemma-2B 62.9-92.4% refusal across adversarial probes (the exact figure the task cites), Gemma-2 highest refusal rate on EtiCor, Gemma 3 12B refusing legitimate professional content (court decisions, clinical notes; GitHub google-deepmind/gemma#595), and community reports calling Gemma 4 'strongly censored' / refusing legitimate medical questions. CRUCIAL COUNTER-EVIDENCE: Google's OFFICIAL Gemma 4 model card states Gemma 4 'significantly outperform[s] Gemma 3 and 3n models in improving safety, while keeping unjustified refusals low' - the first time Google explicitly markets reduced over-refusal, suggesting the historical 62-92% reputation may NOT hold for Gemma 4 31B (but no third-party XSTest score confirms this yet). QWEN SIDE: Qwen3-32B is generally MORE willing to engage Western biosafety / security-research / dual-use chemistry framing, but it heavily censors China-political topics and Chinese metaphysical/cultural content, and reviewers call it 'over-censorship'; some describe Qwen3/3.5 as having 'a very strong refusal rate' unsuitable for unattended batch work, and newer versions 'refuse to guess.' NEITHER has a published XSTest or OR-Bench number at these exact versions. For Labmate's specific topics (biosafety, security research, dual-use chemistry, controversial hypotheses), Qwen is likely the safer default IF those topics are Western-framed and non-political; Gemma 4 MAY now be competitive per the model card but is unproven. Mitigation for either: strong system prompts asserting legitimate research context, or abliterated/uncensored derivatives (G4-MeroMero-26B reportedly 12/100 refusals vs near-100/100 stock; Qwen 'obliterated' variants common) at the cost of all guardrails. [uncertain - no XSTest/OR-Bench numbers for Gemma 4 31B or Qwen3-32B; based on lineage history + Google model-card claim + community reports]
ecosystem_toolchain: Both mature day-one: llama.cpp (GGUF), Ollama, MLX, vLLM, LM Studio, Unsloth. Tool-call parser flags differ - Gemma 4: vLLM --tool-call-parser gemma4 (note 'pythonic' is Gemma 3, gemma4 is correct for Gemma 4, per Labmate CLAUDE.md) with --reasoning-parser gemma4; Qwen3-32B: --tool-call-parser hermes (or qwen3) with --reasoning-parser qwen3. Both expose OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Relevant here because a guard/judge layer (e.g. Qwen3Guard, or an external cross-judge that is NOT Gemma or Qwen per Labmate testing rules) can be bolted on to catch fabricated citations and miscalibrated refusals regardless of brain. Roughly tied.
labmate_relevance: HIGH. The two failure modes named in this item - (A) hallucinating citations/statistics/scientific claims in a paper draft and (B) refusing legitimate sensitive-but-academic queries (biosafety, security research, dual-use chemistry, controversial hypotheses) - are exactly the failure modes that would most damage a research-assistant agent. Factual fabrication destroys trust in paper drafts and reviews; over-refusal silently breaks agentic chains (a brain that refuses mid-loop is hard to debug and blocks legitimate literature work). This is correctly flagged as a first-class concern for Labmate's orchestrator-brain choice.
recommendation: Do not pick the brain on this dimension alone in isolation - but the practical guidance is: prefer Qwen3-32B as the default brain for SENSITIVE-TOPIC academic queries (Western-framed biosafety / security research / dual-use chemistry / controversial hypotheses), because the Gemma lineage's documented over-refusal track record (62.9-92.4% on Gemma-2B, professional-content refusals through Gemma 3) is the bigger known liability for failure mode (B), and Qwen is reported as more cooperative on exactly those Western academic topics (while being avoided for China-political content, which Labmate rarely needs). HOWEVER, this is genuinely UNCERTAIN because (1) Google's official Gemma 4 model card explicitly claims reduced unjustified refusals, which could flip the verdict, and (2) no third-party XSTest/OR-Bench score exists for either model at these versions. The single highest-value action is to RUN XSTest + OR-Bench + a domain dual-use academic probe set against both Gemma 4 31B and Qwen3-32B locally - that measurement would resolve the winner. For failure mode (A) hallucinated citations/stats: BOTH are weak on parametric recall and MUST be wrapped in RAG over a verified paper corpus; enable thinking mode (improves GPQA-style accuracy and adds self-verification); add an external fact-check/judge layer that is neither Gemma nor Qwen (per Labmate testing rules) to flag fabricated references before they reach a draft. Hybrid strategy: Gemma 4 31B for figure-heavy paper reading and reasoned-science (GPQA strength + native vision), Qwen3-32B for sensitive-topic text reasoning where over-refusal would block the workflow - but validate refusal behavior empirically before committing. [uncertain - tipping factor is an unrun XSTest/OR-Bench measurement on both exact models]
